newsitem.title: USA: Clinton unveils new ways to protect worker pensions.
newsitem.headline: Clinton unveils new ways to protect worker pensions.

text.p: President Clinton Tuesday announced new ways to help workers protect their pension plans when they change jobs and then set off on a four-day campaign trip designed to ensure that he keeps his.

The initiative aims to make it easier for workers to "roll over" their pension plans when they move to a new company or to keep their investment options if they choose to leave their money in their old company's retirement plan.

"At a time when we are trying to seize the opportunities of a growing economy, when five million workers with pensions change jobs every year, we have to make it easier for them to save," Clinton said in a brief Oval Office ceremony.

"Today we are saying to the five millon people who change jobs every year ... you've got a lot better chance to take your retirement plan with you and that means more security for American families," he added.

The proposals, which were outlined by the White House last April, were the latest in a string of federal initiatives that Clinton has put forward as he has campaigned for re-election in the Nov. 5 contest with Republican nominee Bob Dole.

Most nationwide opinion polls show Clinton holding a double-digit lead over Dole. A White House official said Clinton would mention the pension initiatives later on Tuesday as he started a campaign trip to Michigan, Illinois, Arizona, Washington and Oregon.
The White House said in a statement that the Treasury Department has acted to help workers roll over retirement savings into a new employer's pension plan in two ways.

First, it removes a barrier to this by advising firms that a qualified pension plan that accepts a rollover that proves to be invalid will not be disqualified if the plan had reasonably concluded that the money involved was eligible.

Second, it said the department has issued a proposed regulation to make clear that accepting rollovers from new workers will generally not hurt a pension plan's ability to meet non-discrimination requirements. These requirements prohibit plans from providing benefits that discriminate in favour of highly paid employees.

Treasury has also issued "administrative guidance" to ensure that employees who choose to leave their pension money with their former employer's retirement plan will not have their investment choices taken away from them. It makes clear that pension plans that offer a broad range of investment choices to active employees may not limit former workers to investment in a money market fund.
